name: struct-alloc
axis: GC pressure — allocating and discarding many short-lived heap structs (binary-trees shape)
n: maxDepth=16, rounds=4 — 58,370,752 two-pointer nodes built, counted and discarded, plus one long-lived depth-16 tree (131,071 nodes)
notes: The recursive node type FORCES a heap allocation per node in every one of the four — Rust must write `Option<Box<Nd>>`, there is no spelling that keeps the nodes on the stack — so this is a genuine allocator-vs-allocator measurement (WasmGC nursery vs V8 scavenger vs CPython refcount vs malloc/free), not a comparison against zero work. This is the benchmark VL WINS outright, and by a wide margin over Rust: a bump-pointer nursery with a tracing collector beats malloc/free-per-node. Scale-verified: doubling `rounds` gives 1.91-2.03x in all four.
